subject: Television & Streaming
title: The Staff Writer to Executive Producer Pipeline
description: A 60-second lesson on The Staff Writer to Executive Producer Pipeline.

hook.text: A TV writer starts as a staff writer and climbs: story editor, producer, co-executive producer, executive producer.

buildup.text: Staff writers pitch ideas but have little authority.

discovery.text: The hierarchy exists because television requires both fresh ideas and experienced oversight.

twist.text: Streaming disrupted the ladder. Shorter seasons mean fewer episodes and fewer jobs.

climax.text: The pipeline from staff writer to showrunner takes a decade of work.

punchline.text: The ladder to the top got shorter—and harder to climb.

quiz.question: How has streaming affected the traditional TV writing career pipeline?
options: Shorter seasons and mini-rooms reduced positions, narrowing the path from staff writer to showrunner
